input.question: How is currency/money in banks and other financial institutions safe-guarded from computer-based attacks?
input.ground_truth: Insane amounts of backups. The record keeping is highly regulated and by law the banks/financial institutions must follow the rules of having the information secured, AND backed up in a number of ways. Worst case scenario, they would have to stop all transactions and fix their databases. Source: I build these systems.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: How is currency/money in banks and other financial institutions safe-guarded from computer-based attacks?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Sure! Here’s how I would explain it to a 5-year-old:

Imagine you have a big toy box full of your favorite toys, and you want to make sure no one can sneak in and take them when you’re not looking. Banks and big money places do the same thing with their “money toys” but they use computers instead of a toy box.

They put their money information inside special computer boxes called “servers.” These servers are like super-strong toy chests with many locks. The locks are called “passwords” and “codes.” Only the grown-ups who are supposed to be in charge know the secret codes.

Also, the computer has special guards called “security systems.” These guards watch all the time and make sure nobody sneaky tries to break in. If someone tries to break in, the guards can tell the grown-ups right away and stop them.

Sometimes, the money information is also hidden using magic tricks called “encryption.” It’s like writing your secret message with invisible ink, so only the people with the special flashlight (the secret key) can see what it says.

So, banks and money places use lots of locks, guards, and magic tricks to keep the money safe from computer bad guys!
